newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF tells Japan politicians don't comment on rates.
newsitem.headline: MOF tells Japan politicians don't comment on rates.

text.p: Japanese politicians should refrain from commenting on interest rates, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a parliamentary committee on Wednesday.
Asked about recent comments by members of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party calling for a rise in the official discount rate, Mitsuzuka said he would like them to refrain from making such comments.

"Monetary policy is wholly in the hands of the Bank of Japan. We are in the midst of discussing a revision of the BOJ law in parliament. I would like them to refrain from making such comments at such a time," he said.
He said worries over an excessive weakening of the yen have completely disappeared.
"A stable currency market is important for the economy. Excessive strengthening of the yen as well as excessive weakening of the yen is undesirable," he said.
"Since April 10, worries over excessive weakening of the yen have completely disappeared," he said.
On that date the dollar rose above 127.16 yen, its highest level since August 1992. It rose above that level to 127.47 yen on May 1, but since then has steeply declined.
At midday on Wednesday in Tokyo the dollar stood at around 114.25 yen.
Mitsuzuka said Japan will keep careful watch over foreign exchange movements and deal "in a timely and appropriate way" with foreign exchange volatility and excessive movements.
